newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai govt says budget cut caused by economic slump.
newsitem.headline: Thai govt says budget cut caused by economic slump.

text.p: Thai deputy finance Minister Chaiyawat Wibulsawat said Thursday a decision to cut government spending in 1997 was caused by the country's economic slowdown.

Chaiyawat told reporters the move was made after careful consideration by the finance ministry which projected revenues might not meet the 984 billion baht (US$39.3 billion) spending set for the 1997 fiscal year starting October 1.
Permanent secretary of finance Chatu Mongol Sonagul said spending will be cut by around 16 billion baht.
Chaiyawat said the decision reflected the government's fiscal discipline and said foreign investors should not be alarmed by the cut.
Thailand needs to maintain a balanced budget policy, Chaiyawat said, adding that the budget deficit would be detrimental to the country's economy.
The finance ministry and the Budget Bureau will soon discuss spending cut details, he said.
The Bank of Thailand forecast that 1996 economic growth will reach 7.8 percent. But many economists predicted actual growth could be below seven percent due to drastic slowdown in exports.
